NoteTexAccessor::limit_norm¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::limit_norm() const

Strip The \limits/\nolimits Position Modifier¶

limit_norm() removes every occurrence of the literal commands \limits and \nolimits — the modifiers that force a following subscript/superscript to render above/below (\limits) or beside (\nolimits) an operator such as \sum, \int, or \max — leaving the operator and its scripts otherwise unchanged. Use it to normalize source that only needs to compare or process the underlying math, not its inline positioning hints.

After both commands are removed, the result passes through the library’s shared whitespace-normalization step: runs of whitespace collapse to a single space and the cell is trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace. This means removing \limits never leaves a double space or stray leading/ trailing gap behind, even though the command itself is deleted with nothing put in its place.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Both Commands, On Different Operators¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\lim\\limits_{x \\to 0} f(x) \\sum\\nolimits_i x_i"})
              .tex().limit_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\lim_{x \\to 0} f(x) \\sum_i x_i"]

\lim\limits_{...} becomes \lim_{...}; \sum\nolimits_i becomes \sum_i.

Example 2: Surrounding Whitespace Collapses¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a \\limits  b"}).tex().limit_norm() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["a b"]

\limits is deleted and the two runs of surrounding whitespace it leaves behind collapse to the single space between a and b.

Example 3: A Shape-Preserving Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\max\\nolimits_x f(x)", "no change"})
              .tex().limit_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\max_x f(x)", "no change"]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().limit_norm().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().limit_norm();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • sum_norm: collapses the separately spelled \sumlimits/\sumnolimits single-command form.

  • int_norm: the equivalent collapse for multi-integral command spellings, an operator this method’s \limits/\nolimits modifiers commonly follow.
